correctness.rationale: For all real and complex n>=3 and 1<=ell<n, invariance reduces the data to two basis vectors, idempotence of Haar P=QQ* gives conditional uniform sphere direction, and U=||Q*e1||^2 is Beta(a,b). The independent Beta(delta,(n-2)delta) coordinate fraction combines with Gamma(b+c) via beta-gamma algebra; independent splitting T/(T+H) produces the claimed Beta(b,c) contraction. Gaussian conditioning gives Gamma(delta)/Gamma(a). Strict order follows from continuous positive beta-prime density and a.s. B<1 when ell>1. Gamma moments show iff q<a, with infinity at q=a included, and density asymptotics plus dominated convergence give the explicit positive tail constant. A standalone direct-sketch and distributional-sampling verifier passed 610 diagnostics; these finite checks do not prove the infinite claims.

value.rationale: First-moment optimality does not control failure probabilities or variance of squared residuals. Exact beta contraction proves a uniform stochastic improvement at every excess-error threshold and every monotone loss, while yielding a sharp finite/infinite moment boundary and a concrete leading tail-constant ratio. This addresses quantitative reliability of two canonical sketching choices in an interpretable scalar baseline. It does not assert a general-rank or implementation theorem.
